questions.title: Practising chips and putts while waiting at the tee
questions.question: Can you practise a chip or a putt on or near the tee box while you wait for your turn to hit?

choices.text: Yes, you can practise chipping or putting there.
No, you have to wait without hitting any shots.
Only if no other players are waiting to play.
Only if your coach is standing with you.

questions.explanation: You can practise chipping or putting on or near the tee box if it is not your turn to play, as long as you do not slow down the game.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A short golf shot to make the ball go softly onto the green.
A soft shot on the green to roll the ball into the hole.
The area where you start a hole and play your first shot.

questions.teachingTip: Let children try a few chip or putt shots near the tee before starting a hole so they know when it is okay. Remind them to be quick so no one has to wait long.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they must always just wait and not play any shots before their turn.
Children might think they can only practise if their coach says so.
Children might believe they can only practise if the teeing area is empty.
